patch_description:
The prior program uses a six-parameter 3-fold ring family with a 300-member differential-evolution population, 570 generations, soft-min finite-difference refinement, and sparse random polish. Its main limitation is that final refinement distributes effort uniformly across all ring parameters even though only a small subset of rings typically participates in the currently limiting triangles.

This version retains the unit-area equilateral hull and deterministic six-parameter representation, but changes the optimization schedule: a larger structured/global population uses a mixed DE/current-to-elite portfolio, followed by an active-constraint bottleneck polish. During polish, the smallest triangle constraints are inspected directly; ring parameters are selected proportionally to their participation in those constraints. The local search includes coordinated radius/phase moves and paired-ring perturbations, while accepting only strict improvements to the exact minimum triangle area. This focuses the fixed evaluation budget on dimensions controlling the active bottlenecks and removes the relatively expensive finite-difference soft-min gradient stage.
